$comment: A derived template (packs/README.md 'Derived templates'): the care pack composed with a direct primary care content seed, re-registered in the wayfinding register (the 1970s transit wayfinding system) with its own pinned page skeletons. Everything else — pages' builders, sections, contract, tests — is the base pack's; compose expands this catalog through resolveCatalog (scripts/lib/pack-switch.mjs).
title: Direct Primary Care
description: A direct primary care practice's site with real online appointment booking: one doctor's membership clinic in a Philadelphia rowhouse — the hero's live open badge and three load-bearing facts ($89/mo, same-day visits, text your doctor), what the membership includes as pictogram rows, a printed membership and at-cost lab price list, the coverage it pairs with (kinds of plans, never insurer logos), house calls, the team with portraits, member reviews, an FAQ (insurance, labs, after-hours, Medicare), hours and a map-ready address, and a booking page that projects each provider's actual weekly availability into concrete bookable times (free meet & greet 15 min, member visit 30, long visit 60) — capacity-1 slots on the managed booking domain, double-booking impossible. The booking form is deliberately clinically empty: name, contact, visit type, new/returning — no symptoms, no health questions; patient health information never touches the site. Five pages, all facts in one content file, art-directed in the wayfinding register: a 1970s transit sign system in forest green, white, and signal yellow.

content.$comment: Business-content contract seed, merged over repobot.content.json at compose (the same overlay path as landing/theme). The practice domain mirrors content.ts codePractice section for section and the appointments domain mirrors codeAppointments entry for entry (the seed-fidelity tests pin both), so the Manage practice editor and provider calendar open on exactly the facts the site already shows, and the platform projects exactly the capacity-1 slots the sandbox simulation offers. The appointments seed is booking mode 2's input: the platform generates a booking_session per provider x window x visit type occurrence, capacity 1, with the provider-wide overlap lock making double-booking impossible.

providers.name: Dr. Ada Okafor
providers.bio: Fourteen years in family medicine, the last five running this practice out of a South 10th Street rowhouse. Ada left a clinic that booked her four patients an hour. Her panel is capped so she can answer your text herself — usually before lunch.

providers.name: Luis Ferreira
providers.bio: Luis handles everything between visits: specialist referrals, prior authorizations, the imaging center that won't call back. He runs the free meet & greets and speaks Portuguese and Spanish.

providers.name: Linh Tran
providers.bio: Linh draws labs in-house, calls with results, and keeps the dispensary of common generics stocked at cost. Ask her which lab panels are $5 — she knows every price by heart.

services.name: Same-day visits
services.description: Text by noon and you're usually seen today, next day at the latest. Thirty minutes minimum, never a waiting room full of strangers.

services.name: Text & call your doctor
services.description: Dr. Okafor's own number. Photos of the rash, questions about the new prescription, the 9 PM "is this normal?" — all included.

services.name: House calls
services.description: For members who can't easily get out: after a hospital stay, with a new baby, or on a bad mobility week. Same doctor, your living room.

services.name: Unhurried visits
services.description: Visits run 30 to 60 minutes. Annual physicals, second opinions, the long talk about a new diagnosis — there's time for all of it.

services.name: Labs at our cost
services.description: Blood work drawn here and billed at the practice's wholesale price. A lipid panel runs about $6; an A1C about $8.

services.name: Chronic care
services.description: Blood pressure, diabetes, thyroid, asthma, depression — steady management by text between visits instead of a three-month wait.

services.name: Minor procedures
services.description: Stitches, skin tag and mole removals, joint injections, ear flushes. Done here, included in the membership, supplies at cost.

services.name: Care coordination
services.description: Referrals to specialists who take your insurance, imaging at cash prices, and someone who reads their notes and calls you after.

reviews.quote: I texted a photo of my son's arm at 7:40 on a Saturday. Dr. Okafor wrote back in ten minutes: not broken, ice it, come by at nine if it swells. It didn't. That's the whole review.
reviews.name: Tasha M.

reviews.quote: My blood work used to cost more than my phone bill. Here the whole panel was eleven dollars and Linh called me with the results the next morning.
reviews.name: Ray D.

reviews.quote: After my hip surgery she came up our front steps with her bag and checked the incision in my own kitchen. I didn't know doctors still did that.
reviews.name: Gloria P.

reviews.quote: An hour for my first physical. Nobody has ever asked me that many questions and then actually waited for the answers.
reviews.name: Sam K.

newPatient.title: Meet us first — free
newPatient.body: Book a 15-minute meet & greet, in the office or by phone. Ask anything; there's no pitch and no paperwork.

newPatient.title: Join online
newPatient.body: Pick a membership, add family members, and set up monthly billing. No enrollment fee, no contract — cancel with 30 days' notice.

newPatient.title: Your first long visit
newPatient.body: An hour with Dr. Okafor: your history, a full exam, and labs drawn on the spot if you need them. You'll leave with her cell number.

newPatient.title: Records & prescriptions
newPatient.body: Sign one release and Luis requests your records. Ongoing prescriptions carry over, and common generics can be filled here at cost.

types.name: Meet & greet (free)
types.description: Fifteen minutes to meet the practice and ask anything before you join.

types.name: Member visit
types.description: A same-day or scheduled visit with Dr. Okafor.

types.name: Long visit
types.description: A physical, a first visit, or the conversation that needs an hour.

theme.$comment: The wayfinding register worn in its own forest green: mode light opens the site in its native daylight appearance (white ground, green sign panels), and the green rides as the project brand so app-side surfaces wear the same register as the marketing pages instead of the kernel default blue. The marketing pages resolve brand over preset accent, so a brand edit re-inks every sign panel — the transit system in a different line color.

landing.$comment: A pinned layout (packs/README.md 'Derived templates'): style re-registers the base's pages in the wayfinding register (forest-green sign panels, signal-yellow rules, heavy grotesk caps, circular pictograms), and pages carries exactly the skeletons careLanding.ts emits from this remix's contentSeed — the content-gated sections (promises, menu, spotlight, faq) appear because the seed fills them — so the composed template's document reproduces its code config section for section (tests/View/Care/careLanding.test.ts reads this through composedLandingSeed).
